content.text: I changed one file, `solution/util.py`, and the visible suite now passes (2 passed). The cause was in `_parse`: it tagged numeric prerelease identifiers as `(1, ident)`, with the digits still stored as a string. That is exactly how it tagged alphanumeric identifiers, so `compare` in `solution/core.py` ordered everything by text, and `"11"` came before `"2"`. The fix tags numeric identifiers as `(0, int(ident))` instead. They now compare by value, and because `0` sorts before `1` they also come before alphanumeric identifiers, which is the precedence order SemVer requires. Since the type tag always differs between the two kinds, Python never has to compare an int against a str.
